qs.q: A medical student is creating flashcards for lysosomal storage diseases. Which substance accumulates in Gaucher disease?
o: GM2 ganglioside accumulating via deficient hexosaminidase
qs.e: Gaucher disease involves a deficiency in glucocerebrosidase leading to the accumulation of glucocerebroside, distinct from mucopolysaccharides found in mucopolysaccharidoses. Confusing these storage products is a frequent exam trap.
qs.s: Clinical Genetics: Master Mendelian Disorders & Molecular Basis: MCQs

qs.q: Gaucher disease involves accumulation of which lipid?
qs.e: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency leads to glucocerebroside accumulation in macrophages.

qs.q: Gaucher's disease, the most common lysosomal storage disease, is caused by deficiency of
qs.e: Autosomal recessive. Gaucher cells = lipid-laden macrophages with "crumpled tissue paper" cytoplasm. Affects liver, spleen (massive), bone marrow. Type 1 (non-neuronopathic) = most common, no CNS involvement. Treatment: enzyme replacement therapy (imiglucerase).
